title: S3: Python module graph and import resolution (ADR 0008)
description: ADR 0008 / DEC-303 (a2) rulings 6, 7: source roots, first-party packages (directory with __init__.py), module identity, absolute/relative/aliased/re-exported import resolution, star imports and __all__, the exit-7 trigger, counted and named unresolved first-party imports. Built on the S2b parse wrapper; bytes only; not wired to the CLI.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Rules per case written before the code and every case has a test
The fixtures-abs absolute-import fixture resolves every first-party import and an unresolvable first-party package root is the exit-7 trigger
Unresolved non-root first-party imports are counted and named, never silent
The S2b inherits are measured: bytes only, wide-node walk cost, column units

implementationNotes: S3 BRIEF (approved by the leader, draft rule list the specialist refines in its first EMPTY commit; R = ruled, D = drafted by the worker as a proposal): 1 roots (D): repo root, src/, lib/, packages/*/src in that order; a file belongs to the deepest listed root containing it; a name in two roots resolves to the first, the shadowed one counted and named; 2 module identity (D): dotted name = path under its root, .py stripped, /__init__.py = the package; only .py indexed, .pyi beside .py ignored and counted; 3 first-party package (R, ruling 6): a directory with __init__.py outside excluded paths (venvs, node_modules, build output, .git, site-packages); never a bare .py or a directory without __init__.py; PEP 420 namespace packages are not first-party (ruled accepted cost); resolving through one is unresolved and counted; 4 absolute import (D): first component against first-party packages by root order then walk; 5 from pkg import name (D): a binding in pkg/__init__.py wins, else submodule, else unresolved first-party counted; 6 relative import (D): dots against the importing file package, too many dots = unresolved counted, never exit 7; 7 aliases (D): record original and alias; 8 re-exports (D): from .x import y in __init__.py binds y, chains followed with a cycle guard (unresolved reason import-cycle); 9 star imports (D): literal __all__ (list/tuple of strings, += literals) else public module-level names; star from a non-first-party module = unresolved bin star-import; 10 conditional imports (D): try/except ImportError, TYPE_CHECKING, platform arms all recorded, two bindings of one name both kept with the condition as reason; 11 external (R): a first component naming no first-party package is external by import binding, no stdlib list; 12 exit 7 (R, ruling 6): an import binds a first-party package (directory with __init__.py) that no root resolves; name the directory and import; every other failed first-party import (missing submodule, generated _pb2, optional extension) is counted and named; 13 dynamic imports (D): importlib.import_module/__import__/getattr not resolved, counted as dynamic; 14 parse errors and decode replacements (S2b inherit): imports inside ERROR regions dropped and the file named; decodeReplacements>0 named; never exact for those files; 15 self-imports and test dirs mirroring package names (D): first root wins, collisions counted and named. S2b INHERITS to MEASURE and commit as text: bytes only (lossy string vs bytes), wide-node cost (child(i) possibly O(i): a 50,000-element list literal, namedChildren vs cursor walk, plus hasError pruning), UTF-8 vs UTF-16 column units on non-ASCII, large-file behaviour (no cap/timeout invented). Interface: buildModuleGraph(files: {path, bytes}[], options) -> module table, per-file import bindings (original, alias, kind, resolved target or reason), counted lists. Feeds: the fixtures-abs fail-closed check and the alias census. Reuse test/python-lsp-measurement/fixtures-abs. No CLI wiring, no cache, no new dependency. Dispatch only after the S2b delta review is clean (stack on feat/GCLI-73-python-parser 1eab226).

S3 landed at 287cc9a (stacked on S2b 206324d plus the --no-ff merge 023a163 of test/GCLI-74-requests-independent; push order S0/S0b before S2b before S3/S4). Verified by the worker under pinned bun 1.4.2: bun run check 337 pass 0 fail (289 before; 48 new tests), lore 0.14.1 check 0/0; package.json and bun.lock untouched. Commits: 9ae9728 rules-first empty commit (17 cases, R: 3, 11, 12; the rest D), a4f61b8 src/python/modules.ts + 48 tests, a62b13e measurements text, 287cc9a two extra tests. fixtures-abs: all 3 bindings in src/app/a.py resolve to src/app/b.py; roots [''] yields the exit-7 trigger naming src/app with 0 resolved. Mutation proofs: exit-7 check red on exactly the two predicted tests, shadow/collision check red on exactly the rule-15 test. S2b inherits measured on generated sources (not click) at a4f61b8, bun 1.4.2: bytes vs string 10.26 vs 10.35 ms (equal; differs only on invalid input); 50,000-element list: namedChildren array 0.14 ms vs namedChild(i) loop 10.43 ms vs child(i) loop 18.46 ms vs cursor walk 12.94 ms (cursor not faster; hot traversal uses the namedChildren getter); columns are UTF-16 code units in this binding (parsePython decodes bytes to a string first; the module graph records only line numbers); large files linear, ~3.2 MB/s up to 3.6 MB, no cap invented. D-RULE AMBIGUITIES to review: outside-roots files named and ignored; intra-root pkg/__init__.py vs pkg.py: package wins, module shadowed and named; namespace-only top dir does not stop the root search; non-literal __all__ gives an unresolved star binding (reason non-literal-all) instead of falling back to public names; getattr counted as dynamic (an upper bound); every .pyi ignored and counted; worker-chosen excluded dir set (.git node_modules dist build out coverage vendor .next .nuxt __pycache__ .venv venv .tox .nox site-packages *.egg-info); packages/*/src roots ordered lexicographically; degenerate <root>/__init__.py yields module name empty string. ACs stay unchecked until review.

OPUS REVIEW RESULT AND RULINGS (relayed by the leader, 2026-11-24): #121 (S3) at head 92f37736a66ff91dbdb45bb8244fc6741a406ba9 returned CHANGES REQUESTED (claude-opus-5-5, read from its transcript; 3 blocking, 9 non-blocking). DEC-303 (a6) on opum-ai/opum-doc (opum-doc ruling, quoted verbatim): "glyph S3 blockers: both arm A. 1. Root candidates are only TOPMOST package directories (__init__.py with no __init__.py in the parent). Ruling 6 and ADR 0008 line 75 are amended to say so. Nested stdlib-named subpackages (django/http, sqlalchemy/ext/asyncio) no longer cause exit 7; a genuinely unresolvable first-party root still does. 2. The guard's first-party set comes from ALL non-excluded candidates whatever roots are declared; declared roots replace the default set for RESOLUTION only, so declaring roots never turns the guard off. Tests both ways for each, including roots ["src"] plus lib/foo/__init__.py, where "import foo" is first-party. The star-import hop and S4's two blockers are the worker's."

WHAT TO DO FOR S3: blocking 1 and 2 per (a6) arm A (amend ADR 0008 line 75 and the ruling-6 wording in the glyph component ADR, quoting (a6)); both with tests both ways (negative test: src/app/__init__.py + src/app/json/__init__.py + src/a.py "import json" must be external; roots ["src"] + lib/foo/__init__.py + src/a.py "import foo" must give a first-party result, not external). Blocking 3 (star hops: propagate the first nested reason, add a two-hop test) is the worker's. Non-blocking: take the cheap ones (5 localeCompare to code-unit compare, 8 depth-limit reason, 4 plain dotted re-export target, 12 minor items and the firstParty flag for namespace packages), memoize (9) only if small, state rule 16/10 limit, and test gaps (6). FULL VERDICT FOLLOWS (verbatim):
# Opus review (claude-opus-5-5, 22 assistant records) of opum-ai/glyph-cli#121 (GCLI-75, S3), head 92f37736a66ff91dbdb45bb8244fc6741a406ba9, base dev bd78650a — VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

## BLOCKING
1. Exit 7 fires falsely when a stdlib or external name matches a nested subpackage. src/python/modules.ts:1307-1316 builds packageRootsByBase from every __init__.py directory, subpackages included. findTop (:841-842) then turns any unresolved top-level name that matches a subpackage's basename into exit 7.
 - Trace: src/app/__init__.py + src/app/json/__init__.py + src/a.py "import json" gives unresolved-package-root and an exit-7 entry. It should be external (R rule 11).
 - Real cases: Django has django/http/ and imports "from http import cookies". SQLAlchemy has ext/asyncio/ and imports asyncio. Both would go indeterminate even though their roots are correct.
 - Declaring a root does not fix it. Declaring one at the subpackage's parent would make it wrong.
 - click and requests are flat, so fixtures-abs, the gate and the 48 tests cannot see this.
 - Fix: candidates are only the topmost package directories (the parent holds no __init__.py). The rule-12 test (tools/other) still passes under that rule. Add a negative test.
 - ADR 0008 line 75 says "anywhere in the repository tree". If the worker reads that literally, the ADR wording is the defect and it routes to opum-doc. Either way the slice should not ship as written.
 -> LEADER: this one and #2 are routed to opum-doc as an A/B (my recommendation A for both); do NOT change root semantics until the ruling is relayed.
2. Declared roots switch off the exit-7 guard for packages outside them, which is the silent-loss mode the ADR cites (layouts.txt, 0/5).
 - :1197-1203 drops files outside the declared roots to ignored/outside-roots. packageRootsByBase (:1308) and FileIndex (:1320) are built only from `indexed`.
 - Trace: roots ["src"], lib/foo/__init__.py, src/a.py "import foo" gives outcome external, with no exit 7 and no unresolved count. The only trace is lib/foo/*.py listed in ignored.
 - Declaring roots is exactly the remedy ruling 6 prescribes for exit 7 ("until a root is declared"), so the guard must still work afterwards.
 - It also conflicts with ruling 10 ("every .py outside excluded paths is indexed"): with declared roots, every other .py is dropped from the index.
 - Fix: build the first-party package set from all non-excluded candidates, not from indexed files. Separately, rule whether declared roots add to the defaults or replace them.
 -> LEADER: held for opum-doc's ruling (see above).
3. The star-import bins hold for one hop only, so a partial star set is reported as complete.
 - moduleExports (:1024-1031) silently skips a nested star whose outcome is external or unresolved, and drops nested.reason.
 - Trace: m.py = "from os import *\ndef f(): pass" (no __all__); use.py = "from m import *". The binding comes out outcome resolved, reason null, starNames ["f"], which claims a complete set.
 - Same result when n has a non-literal __all__ and m does "from n import *".
 - In resolveName (:960-961), a name that could come from such a star comes out attribute-not-found, which is the wrong reason.
 - So the worker's non-literal-all refinement (no fallback to public names) is sound and stated at one level, and correctly tested there (test:302). It is not carried transitively, and decision 7 needs it to be.
 - Fix: propagate the first nested reason (star-import / non-literal-all / import-cycle) to the outer export set, and test a two-hop chain. (IMPLEMENTATION: do this.)

## NON-BLOCKING
4. modules.ts:969-970: a re-export of a plain dotted import resolves to the wrong target. moduleBindingResolution returns the leaf file for "import a.b", but the bound name is "a", which is a/__init__.py. So "from m import a", where m does "import a.b", resolves silently to a/b.py. If m does both "import a.b" and "import a.c", it comes out as a spurious multiply-bound.
5. :1327 orders bindings with localeCompare, which depends on the host locale/ICU. Everywhere else the file uses code-unit `<`. Use the same here.
6. Test gaps: (a3) Q2 multiply-bound (collapseNameResolutions :717-738) is never asserted (suggested case: pkg/__init__.py with try "from .fast import f" / except "from .slow import f", then "from pkg import f"; assert reason multiply-bound and alternatives). Within-root pkg.py vs pkg/__init__.py (package wins, module shadowed, :1257-1261) has no test. The nested pkg/sub.py vs pkg/sub/__init__.py case is not counted at all: walkFrom prefers the package, but :1248 only considers top-level entries (a silent shadow). "packages/*/src roots are discovered and sorted" (test:48) sorts its own output before comparing, so it does not check root order. No test checks that permuting the input gives identical output. No three-dot relative import test.
7. :336/:636 match the callee text literally. "from importlib import import_module; import_module(x)" (the common Django form) and an aliased importlib are missed. The "counted as an upper bound" claim holds for getattr but not for import_module.
8. :948 caps depth at 64 and reports import-cycle for a deep chain that is not a cycle; it should report something like depth-limit.
9. resolveName and moduleExports use path-scoped visited sets (deleted in finally) with no memoization. Re-export and star DAGs with diamonds re-explore shared subgraphs, so the worst case is exponential and every from-import re-walks it. The measurements only cover parse throughput, not resolver scale. Memoize completed export sets. Not blocking while the module is unwired.
10. Function- and class-local imports are only recorded as text (rule 16). They are never resolved and never checked for exit 7, so an unrooted package imported only lazily never triggers it. State this as a rule or close the gap.
11. Excluded directories match by name at any depth (:267-270). The coverage.py repo's own coverage/ package and pypa/build's src/build/ package would be ignored as excluded-path, and their self-imports would then come out external rather than exit 7. Named, so not silent, but the worker-chosen set should match only at the root, or skip directories holding __init__.py.
12. Minor: __all__.extend(...) and __all__.append(...) are ignored, so the export set is incomplete with reason null. The elif/else condition text reads "ifcond && elif X" and "ifcond && else". namedChild(i) loops remain at :380 and :493 (narrow nodes, harmless). The graph's `exact` stays true while exit7 is non-empty (the wiring slice must check exit7.length; consider an explicit indeterminate flag). An unresolved namespace-package import is labelled firstParty: true although rule 3 says namespace packages are not first-party.

## VERIFIED BY READING
Scope: only .quest/tasks/GCLI-75.json, src/python/modules.ts, test/python-modules-measurements.txt, test/python-modules.test.ts; package.json, bun.lock, .github and other src untouched; no new dependency. modules.ts imports only parse.ts and a type; no fs/network/cache. Trees freed in a finally (:1289-1294), only strings retained. Resolution correct for: relative level handling (too-many-dots and no-package; too-many-dots never reaches exit 7), package-before-module in findTop and walkFrom, from-import order (binding, then submodule, then attribute-not-found), `from . import x` self-exclusion in __init__.py, alias recording, every branch arm walked (TYPE_CHECKING, platform, try/except), decode replacements and ERROR-region drops named and counted. Output ordering does not depend on input order (indexed sorted at :1213), apart from the localeCompare (finding 5) and which duplicate's bytes win (named). Measurements arithmetic consistent: 10.43/0.14 about 75x, 12.94/0.14 about 92x; the module graph records only row+1; bytes-only holds.
